messages:
cheng: Heads-up — noticed a p99 spike on the chat-serving fleet around 11:10. Telemetry dump shows many requests getting dispatched to 'generic_matmul_fallback' when effective_seq > 2048. https://logs.example.com/trace/1965432100 :eyes:

sam: I pulled the same trace. Looks like autotuner switched away from the fast kernel due to workspace checks failing on A100-80. There's a 'kernel_workspace_needed' reason in the pick log.

maria: Dumped picktrace from the node:
```
PICK: fast_matmul_v2 @ arch=a100, seqlen=2300, workspace_needed=117M, workspace_available=64M, reason=workspace_too_small
PICK: generic_matmul_fallback @ reason=fallback_workspace
```
Looks like the workspace calc rounded down somewhere.

lee: To confirm, KV cache counts toward effective sequence length. If users have large conversation prefixes cached, seqlen can jump. We should add a telemetry field that separates input_seq vs kv_cache_seq.

perf-bot: Perf run #378 for commit abc123 -> p99 increased from 118ms to 215ms on a100-scale test (load: chat-1000). Regression flagged.

sam: Repro locally with a small harness: when MODEL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT env is set low (32MB) the autotuner chooses fallback quickly. Debug flags that help: `RUNTIME_PICK_DEBUG=1`, `PICK_REASON=verbose`, `LOG_PICK_WORKSPACE=1`.

cheng: Is this safe to hotfix by flipping autotune off for the pool? We need to avoid risk to other customers.

maria: I'm preparing a tiny patch to fix the workspace computation — it used 32-bit arithmetic in one path. Will also emit `pick_workspace_size_bytes` in the telemetry. Patch branches: `fix/workspace-int64` and I'll open a canary PR.

sam: Meanwhile I toggled `AUTOTUNE_DISABLE=1` on serve-eu-a100-canary (just that pool). If the rollback reduces p99 we can rollout a conservative config.

oncall-bot: Rolling restart scheduled for pool `serve-eu-a100-canary` at 11:45 (drain -> restart -> verify). Ticket: #INC-2026.

lee: Also propose adding these telemetry keys ASAP: `input_seq_len`, `kv_cache_len`, `effective_seq_len`, `pick_workspace_needed`, `pick_workspace_available`, `pick_reason`. That will let post-hoc slicing in console.

maria: Agree. I'll add the keys plus a compact pick_reason enum to keep log size small. Example schema in logs: `pick:{kernel:"fast_matmul_v2",reason:"workspace_short",ws_needed:117_000_000,ws_avail:64_000_000}`

cheng: Good. After patch lands can someone run the autotune job with `RUNTIME_PICK_DEBUG=1` and `FORCE_PROFILE=true` across 2 instances? We need a perf run before/after.

perf-bot: Kicked off perf job #379 (tags: canary, pick-debug). Will post results here when done.

sam: FYI — found one additional place where quantization padded workspace was mis-estimated for packed-bias kernels. I'll include that in the PR.

maria: Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2412. Added tests for 64-bit workspace math + extra telemetry. Canarying now.

cheng: Thanks. If the canary looks stable we should roll to serve-eu and then remaining A100 pools. Ping here for rollback window. :thumbsup:

sam: If anyone hits a lingering p99 after the fix, please paste the full pick log (use `RUNTIME_PICK_DEBUG=1`) and tag me. Small, fast threads are easiest to debug.

lee: Note for follow-up: batching heuristics also sometimes coerce requests into longer effective sequences if prefix coalescing kicks in. We should log `batch_prefix_coalesced=true/false`.

maria: Added both keys to the telemetry PR. Will monitor perf-bot results and can push hotfix to prod if canary passes.

perf-bot: Perf job #379 completed: p99 improved from 215ms -> 122ms on canary (baseline before fix: 118ms). No other regressions detected in the sampled tests.

cheng: Excellent. Thanks everyone — closing the loop here.
